speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your episodes of unresponsiveness and facial grimacing, could you describe exactly what happens right before and during these events? Specifically, do you lose awareness completely, and how long do these episodes typically last?

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes lasting 3–4 minutes each of facial grimacing and staring over the past month. During these episodes, he is nonresponsive and does not recall them afterward. He reports a muddy taste in his mouth before the onset of these episodes. His brother witnessed him waking up, staring, and making hand gestures during one episode. The patient felt lethargic and confused afterwards.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the patient have a history of seizures or a family history of epilepsy, and have there been any recent head injuries or infections? I would like to order an EEG to look for abnormal electrical activity in the brain. REQUEST TEST: EEG

speaker: Doctor
text: The EEG findings strongly suggest focal seizures originating in the right temporal lobe. Given the olfactory aura, automatisms, and post-ictal confusion, this clinical picture is classic for temporal lobe epilepsy. DIAGNOSIS READY: Temporal Lobe Epilepsy
